sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
The window was not smooth: revenue growth jumped to 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022 before slowing to 5.0% in FY2024 and re-accelerating to 10.1% in FY2026 [D189][D238][D336][D434].

FY2021's 18% net sales increase came from a 16% comparable sales gain, with strong non-foods and e-commerce, and FY2022's 16% gain from 14% comparable sales plus gasoline, business centers and travel [P56][P42].
FY2026's 10% net sales increase was primarily attributable to an 8% comparable sales gain, with 5% from average ticket and 3% from shopping frequency [P14].
The United States carried the model, contributing 12.2pp of FY2022 growth and 7.2pp of FY2026 growth at a 72.5% revenue share [D474][D672][D670].
In FY2026 warehouse ancillary and other businesses contributed 3.7pp on 19.9% growth, Food and Sundries 2.6pp and Non-Foods 2.2pp [D601][D600][D560][D576].
Membership fees grew 11.0% in FY2026 on new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades, with renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada [D664][P13].
Operating income grew 12.5% in FY2026 against 10.1% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
Operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue in FY2026, at 10.2% cost of revenue growth and 8.9% SG&A growth [D458][D449][D450].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, its window high, against a 3.4% median and 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 bridge was flat on cost of revenue and plus 0.1pp on SG&A, with other lines at minus 0.0pp [D459][D460][D461].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of net sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency adding $126 million [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.8pp below the 3.9% operating margin, the same gap as FY2025 [F52][F32][D732].

Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026, above the 1.75x window median's level only in the sense that it sits below it, and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x [F82][F42][D421][D722][F102][D422].
The increase in operating cash flow was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% was above the 2.8% window median but below the 3.6% high, with capex at 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [D418][D698][D697][D417][D423].
Investing outflow rose to $6.4 billion from $5.3 billion, primarily related to capital expenditures [F112][F111][P5].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, against a -18.3% peer median and the 100th percentile of four retail peers [D427][D428][D734][D733].
Cash and investments grew 39.4% while total debt rose 6.5% to $6.2 billion, leaving long-term debt down 31.5% [D453][D454][D426][D445].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [D429][D430][D452].
FY2026 repurchases totaled $847 million, leaving $1.1 billion available under the program [P3].

Operating margin of 3.9% sits at the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% peer median, and net margin of 3.0% also at the 17th percentile against 3.5% [F32][D709][D710][F52][D711][D712].

The thin-margin model is structural rather than deteriorating, since the 3.9% is the window high, but it leaves little room if cost of revenue, at 87.2% of revenue, moves against the company [F32][D413].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% sits at the 50th percentile against a 4.2% peer median, below it despite the net cash cushion [D418][D713][D714].
Cash generation is adequate but not a differentiator against peers, so the balance-sheet strength rather than conversion is the competitive edge.
Whether operating margin holds at or above the 3.9% FY2026 high or slips toward the 3.4% window median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691][D692].
Whether free cash flow margin stays above the 2.8% window median or falls toward the 1.5% FY2022 low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D698][D696].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue holds above the 5.0% FY2026 level or reverses toward the 2.1% FY2024 level, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D428][D330].
